summary:
The bullpen category is the clearest signal on the board today, running hot across all three ratings — R1, R2, and R3 all sit at 109-79 or 110-78 (58-59%) over the last 14 days versus a season baseline near 51%, a swing of roughly +7pts in each case. Pair that with the trends+runs combo (56.5%, 208-160, n=368), the single best category agreement on the board, and you've got a solid foundation for today's plays. The flip side is the SP category, which is bleeding across the board — all three ratings show it cold, with R1 and R2 down to 42% (79-109) over the last 14 days, a 7.9pt drop from season norms, and R3 at 45% (84-104). Avoid leaning on starting-pitcher-driven picks regardless of rating, and be aware the bullpen_fatigue metric is riding an 8-game losing streak across all three ratings at just 48% — that's a category to fade entirely right now.

On the unit P/L side, R3 is the strongest performer over the last 14 days at 41-40 (+8.0u) and remains the season leader at +35.0u (130-111, 54%), making it the rating to trust most when strong-play flags fire. R1 isn't far behind at +9.0u over 14 days and +27.0u season, while R2 is treading water — 41-42 (+6.0u) over 14 days but a flat -1.0u over the last 30. Team-wise, ride TBR hard when the model likes them: 23-8 (74%) overall and an elite 18-4 (82%, +23.0u) in strong-play spots — the best team angle on the board. BOS (76%, n=33) and CHC (75%, n=24) are also chalk-worthy, but fade HOU strong plays, which are bleeding at 2-7 (22%, -8.0u) despite a respectable overall record — a clear split between the model's base picks and its high-confidence flags on that team.
